# External Video Guide {#videos}

This page lists the external videos that the course uses. Every clip has one
of three purposes:

- **Required before class:** watch it before the lecture. These clips are also
  listed in that lecture's **Video preparation** box.
- **Review when needed:** the clip explains a concept from the lecture material. Use it
  after the lecture, after an absence, or before practice if you do not yet
  understand the concept well.
- **Optional extension:** the clip adds another example or more depth. It is not
  required.

Only clips labelled **Required before class** are compulsory preparation.
Review and extension clips add no exam material. If a video differs from
this textbook in scope or notation, follow the textbook. QM Basic mainly uses
MIT OpenCourseWare pages, which include videos and transcripts. QM
Intermediate uses Stanford's Statistical Learning series. The complete collections are the
[MIT probability playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLUl4u3cNGP60hI9ATjSFgLZpbNJ7myAg6)
and the
[Stanford Statistical Learning playlist](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLoROMvodv4rOzrYsAxzQyHb8n_RWNuS1e).

## Supplementary probability reading

MIT OpenCourseWare offers Bertsekas and Tsitsiklis's
[Introduction to Probability: Selected Textbook Summary Material](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/introduction-to-probability-selected-textbook-summary-material/).
The official page includes the
[PDF download](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/d973b10c2587781f86ca4f2aff49098f_MITRES_6_012S18_Textbook.pdf).
This 77-page text is a reference, not required reading. Read only a section
that a lecture asks you to read, or that you need for review.

## Basic Lecture 1: Introduction to data analysis

No external video is assigned. The lecture chapter lists the preparation.

## Basic Lecture 2: Probability foundations and random variables

**Required before class**

- [01.2 Sample Space](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/sample-space/):
  outcomes, sample spaces, and events.
- [01.4 Probability Axioms](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/probability-axioms/):
  non-negativity, normalisation, and additivity.
- [05.2 Definition of Random Variables](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/definition-of-random-variables/):
  a random variable as a function from outcomes to numbers.

**Review when needed**

- [01.3 Sample Space Examples](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/sample-space-examples/):
  more examples of outcomes and events.
- [01.5 Simple Properties of Probabilities](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/simple-properties-of-probabilities/):
  complement and addition rules derived from the axioms.
- [01.10 Interpretations and Uses of Probabilities](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/interpretations-uses-of-probabilities/):
  how the meaning of a probability depends on the model.

**Optional extension**

- [01.7 A Discrete Example](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/a-discrete-example/):
  a worked discrete probability model.

## Basic Lecture 3: Discrete distributions, expectation, and variance

**Required before class**

- [05.3 Probability Mass Functions](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/probability-mass-functions/):
  point probabilities and the normalisation rule.
- [05.8 Expectation](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/expectation/):
  expectation as a probability-weighted average.

**Review when needed**

- [05.4 Bernoulli and Indicator Random Variables](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/bernoulli-indicator-random-variables/):
  coding an event as 1 and its complement as 0.
- [06.2 Variance](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/variance/):
  expected squared distance from the mean. This lecture teaches variance
  and the standard deviation.

## Basic Lecture 4: Conditioning, Bayes' rule, and independence

**Required before class**

- [02.2 Conditional Probabilities](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/conditional-probabilities/):
  limiting attention to the outcomes in the condition and rescaling their
  probabilities.
- [02.8 Bayes' Rule](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/bayes-rule/):
  reversing a condition using base rates and likelihoods.

**Review when needed**

- [02.6 The Multiplication Rule](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/the-multiplication-rule/):
  writing a joint probability with a conditional probability.
- [02.7 Total Probability Theorem](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/total-probability-theorem/):
  combining conditional probabilities across a partition (groups that do
  not overlap and together cover all outcomes).
- [03.3 Independence of Two Events](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/independence-of-two-events/):
  the conditional and product definitions of event independence, which this
  lecture covers.

**Optional extension**

- [02.3 A Die Roll Example](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/a-die-roll-example/):
  a worked conditioning example.

## Basic Lecture 5: Joint random variables, covariance, and correlation

**Required before class**

- [06.7 Joint PMFs and the Expected Value Rule](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/joint-pmfs-and-the-expected-value-rule/):
  joint probabilities and expectations involving two variables.
- [12.5 Covariance](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/covariance/):
  covariance as an expected product of deviations.
- [12.8 The Correlation Coefficient](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/the-correlation-coefficient/):
  standardising covariance.

**Review when needed**

- [07.2 Conditional PMFs](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/conditional-pmfs/):
  the distribution of one variable at a fixed value of another variable.
- [07.4 Independence of Random Variables](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/independence-of-random-variables/):
  checking whether every joint probability equals the product of the two
  corresponding marginal probabilities.
- [12.10 Interpreting the Correlation Coefficient](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/interpreting-the-correlation-coefficient/):
  what correlation does and does not describe.

**Optional extension**

- [12.6 Covariance Properties](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/covariance-properties/):
  additional algebraic properties of covariance.

## Basic Lecture 6: Continuous distributions and the normal model

**Required before class**

- [08.2 Probability Density Functions](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/probability-density-functions/):
  density, area, and interval probability.
- [08.3 Uniform and Piecewise Constant PDFs](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/uniform-piecewise-constant-pdfs):
  constant density over an interval.
- [08.8 Normal Random Variables](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/normal-random-variables/):
  normal shape and parameters.

**Review when needed**

- [08.9 Calculation of Normal Probabilities](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/calculation-of-normal-probabilities/):
  standardisation and normal interval probabilities.
- [08.7 Cumulative Distribution Functions](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/cumulative-distribution-functions/):
  cumulative probability for discrete and continuous variables.

## Basic Lecture 7: Samples, parameters, and estimators

The MIT clips for Lectures 7 to 9 write $M_n$ for the sample mean, which
this book writes $\bar X$, and $\hat\Theta$ for an estimator.

**Required before class**

- [20.3 The Sample Mean and Some Terminology](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/the-sample-mean-and-some-terminology/):
  parameters, estimators, estimates, and the sample mean.

## Basic Lecture 8: Sampling distributions and the central limit theorem

**Required before class**

- [19.2 The Central Limit Theorem](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/the-central-limit-theorem/):
  the normal approximation for standardised sums and means.

## Basic Lecture 9: The t distribution and confidence intervals

**Required before class**

- [20.5 Confidence Intervals](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/confidence-intervals/):
  what "95% confidence" means over repeated samples.
- [20.7 Confidence Intervals for the Mean When the Variance Is Unknown](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/confidence-intervals-for-the-mean-when-the-variance-is-unknown/):
  replacing $\sigma$ by the sample standard deviation and using a t distribution. This
  lecture starts with the t distribution.
- [Introduction to Hypothesis Testing](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ti9NFdjf3sM):
  the null model, a two-sided alternative, and the p-value.

**Review when needed**

- [20.6 Confidence Intervals for the Estimation of the Mean](https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/res-6-012-introduction-to-probability-spring-2018/resources/confidence-intervals-for-the-estimation-of-the-mean/):
  the interval for the mean when the variance is known. It is background
  for the interval with unknown variance that the lecture uses.

## Basic Lecture 10: Testing decisions, errors, power, and a first look at regression

**Required before class**

- [Introduction to Hypothesis Testing](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=ti9NFdjf3sM):
  review the null model, two-sided alternatives, and p-values. One-sided
  alternatives are optional reading in this lecture and are not part of the
  exam.
- [Examples Identifying Type I and Type II Errors](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JNOWWJeZBTc):
  decision errors in context.

## Intermediate videos

All required Intermediate clips come from Stanford's Statistical Learning
series and belong to Chapter 3 of *An Introduction to Statistical Learning*.

### Intermediate Lecture 1: Simple linear regression

**Required before class**

- [3.1 Simple Linear Regression](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vCHtY6Me5FI):
  population and fitted lines, least squares, coefficients.

### Intermediate Lecture 2: What the model assumes and how residuals reveal it

No external video is assigned. The preparation is the R warm-up in the
lecture chapter.

### Intermediate Lecture 3: Coefficient inference, fit, and the F-test

**Required before class**

- [3.2 Hypothesis Testing and Confidence Intervals](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3GiWpRfkSjc):
  standard errors, intervals, and tests against zero for a slope. The video
  writes RSS for the quantity this book calls SSE.

### Intermediate Lecture 4: Multiple regression and what controls do

**Required before class**

- [3.3 Multiple Linear Regression](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=o9hoLdylWKo):
  several predictors and conditional coefficients.

**Review when needed**

- [3.4 Some Important Questions](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=50sv4UTjE90):
  fit and prediction questions with several predictors.

### Intermediate Lecture 5: Categories as predictors and joint tests

**Required before class**

- [3.5 Extensions of the Linear Model](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dEBQmiXv9fk):
  qualitative predictors and model extensions.

### Intermediate Lecture 6: Interactions and curvature

**Required before class**

- [3.5 Extensions of the Linear Model](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dEBQmiXv9fk):
  interactions and qualitative predictors.
- [7.1 Polynomials and Step Functions](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=F-D3lZzYn50):
  polynomial terms and non-linear fitted relationships.

**Optional extension for Intermediate**

- [3.R Regression in R](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gNZfqHhq_B4):
  a longer Stanford R lab covering Chapter 3.

External sources may use different notation or cover more material. For what
the course covers, follow this textbook, the formula sheet or code sheet, and
the exam instructions.
